`is_mostly_bin` no longer raises `IndexError` on inputs of 101–103 bytes. I haven't run the tests.

**Cause:** when the input is longer than 100 bytes, the function looks at `s[100]` through `s[103]` to find a spot to cut that doesn't split a UTF-8 character. If the input is only 101–103 bytes and those tail bytes are continuation bytes (`0b10xxxxxx`), the loop indexed past the end of the data.

**Fix:** in `mitmproxy/utils/strutils.py`, the continuation-byte check now reads `cut < len(s) and (s[cut] >> 6) == 0b10`. Reaching the end of the input counts as a character boundary, and the slice `s[:cut]` then keeps the whole input. Inputs of 100 bytes or fewer, or of 104 or more, take the same path as before, so their results don't change.

**Test:** in `test/mitmproxy/utils/test_strutils.py`, I added cases for `101 * b"\x80"`, `102 * b"\x80"` and `103 * b"\x80"`, which previously raised `IndexError`. All three should return `True` (binary).
